I'm identifying the two colored piece shapes—an L-shaped piece with 4 cells and a T-shaped piece with 5 cells, totaling 9 cells—then checking the grey regions to see if a 2x3 block of 6 cells matches up.

Checking further, a 9-cell grey region at rows3-6 does match: splitting it into a top L-shape (row of 3 with one below the leftmost) and a bottom T-shape (row of 3 with two extending below the middle) lines up perfectly with the two given pieces. The other candidate regions (6, 8, 5, and 4 cells) don't fit, so I've found my match and will erase the placeholder colors and recolor that region.

content.text:
I'm sketching out three example inputs with similar structure — trying a pair of pieces like an L-tromino and a 2x2 square totaling 7 cells, then considering a simpler version using a domino and single cell to generate all triomino assemblies.

For the second pair, I'm testing two dominoes as pieces, checking which tetrominoes can be split into two dominoes (line, square, S/Z shapes work, but the T-tetromino can't be split this way, so it stays grey). I'm now working out grid coordinates and placements for the first example, positioning the colored pieces and the grey/colored target shapes so they don't touch each other.

For the third pair, I'm using an L-tromino plus a domino as building pieces to form pentominoes, checking which pentomino shapes can and can't be decomposed this way — confirming the X-pentomino (plus shape) can't be split into a domino and an L-tromino cleanly, so it stays grey, while checking the straight I5 line similarly.

Now I'm laying out the actual grid coordinates for each pair, placing colored and grey pieces cell by cell across the different puzzle boards.

Continuing the grey P-pentomino placement, then adding an X-shaped plus piece and a vertical I5 line in another column. I'm also working out the grey L5 piece, splitting it into a domino plus an L-tromino to make the shape fit correctly.
